top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are an original invention, the magic-wavelength trap, that was experimentally realised and then independently reproduced in laboratories in several countries with agreement at the 1e-18 level, and it opens measurements that could not be made before. The two-name allocation follows the proposal and first realisation (Katori) and the accuracy and many-body frontier (Ye), and the citation stays on the lattice clock itself and not on a record that will be superseded. The topological insulator prize (P002) is strong and well verified but leaves out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed the HgTe system that was measured, and the 3D discovery, so its allocation is less clean; I rank it second and above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no co-authorship, supervision or institutional tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. Chalmers colleague Johansson and nearby Mehlig are institutional connections only.
